scope: model_62_actual_findings_recheck; supplied full current source/tests and explicitly labeled integration diff if present

findings.title: Success-path usage observer failure returns accounting receipt without persisting unconfirmed accounting status
findings.issue: When usage_observer raises after an accepted transport, the code now returns a frozen ModelAccountingReceipt with usage_recorded=False, cost None and accounting_status='unconfirmed' (as claimed), but the exception is swallowed silently and nothing records the accounting failure durably; a caller that drops the returned object loses the fact that accounting is unconfirmed while the operation was already settled accepted with charged upper_bound. This keeps the reply and non-retry semantics but leaves accounting unconfirmed only in-memory.
findings.fix: Persist an accounting-unconfirmed marker or durable accounting attempt record keyed by attempt_ref/operation_refs before returning, and surface the observer failure through a typed non-retryable accounting exception or receipt field that survives process boundaries.

findings.title: Accepted settlement loss path discards typed transport error and returns accepted receipt even when the settled outcome may be unknown
findings.issue: If execute_reserved_groups raises after accepted_reply was observed (e.g. settlement loss wrapped as ScopeTransportUnknown), the code converts it into an accepted receipt with accounting_status='unconfirmed' and retry_allowed=False on the returned object. However ModelAccountingReceipt is a plain frozen dataclass; if a caller checks delivery_outcome/usage_recorded only, it may treat the call as fully settled despite policy settling possibly left as unknown, and no durable marker distinguishes accepted-with-unconfirmed-accounting from accepted-and-settled.
findings.fix: Make the accounting-unconfirmed outcome explicit and durable (status field persisted or exception carrying receipt), and ensure downstream result reporting distinguishes accepted-but-unconfirmed from normal accepted.

findings.title: Preparation-unknown path assigns error attributes to ScopePreparationUnknown without guaranteeing type for callers
findings.issue: ScopePreparationUnknown is re-raised after mutation of attempt_ref/external_call_attempted=False, preserving the class and no-retry semantics as claimed. But the class definition in policy.py does not declare these fields, so any serialized/logged copy of the exception loses external_call_attempted and attempt_ref, risking classification drift in reporting.
findings.fix: Extend ScopePreparationUnknown (or a typed wrapper) with attempt_ref/external_call_attempted as constructor fields so serialization and downstream handling cannot drop them.

findings.summary: The #62 P1s are largely addressed in control code: ScopePreparationUnknown is preserved with non-retry refs and external_call_attempted=False, other pre-HTTP failures become distinct ModelPreparationUnknown without resetting the fence, and a positively observed reply survives later settlement/observer failures via a frozen ModelAccountingReceipt carrying the actual accepted text/model/tokens with usage_recorded=False, cost None, accounting_status='unconfirmed', exact refs and retry_allowed=False. Known invalid responses remain separately typed with no-retry even when the usage observer fails. Remaining P1s concern durability/classification of accounting-unconfirmed and accepted-settlement-loss outcomes and typed serialization of preparation-unknown fields; these are fail-closed for retry but weaken accounting honesty and reporting, so fix before ship.
